title: Graph Neural Networks Automated Design and Deployment on Device-Edge Co-Inference Systems
problem: Naive partitioning of Graph Neural Networks across device-edge systems fails to achieve efficient co-inference due to computational-communication overheads of GNN operations on heterogeneous devices. Jointly optimizing both the GNN architecture and the operation-to-device mapping is essential.
motivation: Device-edge co-inference can significantly improve inference efficiency by strategically distributing computation between resource-constrained devices and powerful edge servers.
method: GCoDE automatically co-designs GNN architecture and operation-to-device mapping in a unified optimization space. It abstracts device communication as an explicit fusible operation, uses constraint-based performance-aware search to evaluate efficiency across heterogeneous systems, and implements a co-inference runtime engine with adaptive dispatcher for deployment.
key_novelty: Joint optimization of GNN architecture and device-edge operation mapping in a unified search space, treating inter-device communication as an explicit fusible operation.
contributions: First automatic co-design framework for GNNs jointly optimizing architecture search and operation mapping across device-edge hierarchies
Communication-as-operation abstraction enabling fusion-based joint optimization
Performance-aware constraint-based search for efficient evaluation on diverse heterogeneous systems
Co-inference engine and runtime dispatcher for practical heterogeneous deployment
primary_theme: Automated GNN co-design for device-edge inference
